text: In June 2023, five people climbed into a tiny sub to visit the Titanic. None came back.
It was called Titan. Its hull was carbon fibre, never proven that deep.
It was steered with a video game controller.
An hour and forty-five minutes into the dive, over three kilometres down, it went silent.
For four days, the world searched, counting down their oxygen.
But the people inside were already gone.
At that depth, the water pushes with more than three hundred times the pressure at the surface.
When the hull gave way, Titan collapsed in a few thousandths of a second.
Its pieces were found on the sea floor, about five hundred metres from the Titanic's bow.
A hundred and eleven years after the Titanic, the same ocean took five more.
